subject: design-technology
source_note: Topic structure follows the Eduqas/WJEC GCSE Design and Technology specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Technical Principles
units.blurb: Core knowledge of materials, systems and our designed world

units.name: Designing & Making Principles
units.blurb: The skills and processes of designing and making

units.name: Design & Make Task (NEA)
units.blurb: Applying principles in a sustained design and make project

topics.name: Design & Technology and Our World
topics.blurb: New and emerging technologies, energy, ecological and social impact

topics.name: Smart Materials & Composites
topics.blurb: Smart materials, composites and technical textiles

topics.name: Electronic Systems & Programmable Components
topics.blurb: Inputs, processes and outputs in control systems

topics.name: Materials
topics.blurb: Sources, properties and applications of material groups

topics.name: In-Depth Material Specialism
topics.blurb: Detailed study of one chosen material area (e.g. timber, metals, polymers, textiles)

topics.name: Investigating Design Possibilities
topics.blurb: Contexts, user needs and primary/secondary research

topics.name: Brief & Specification
topics.blurb: Writing design briefs and specifications from research

topics.name: Generating & Developing Ideas
topics.blurb: Design strategies, communication and iterative development

topics.name: Making Prototypes
topics.blurb: Tools, processes and manufacture of fit-for-purpose prototypes

topics.name: Analysing & Evaluating
topics.blurb: Testing, feedback and reasoned design decisions

topics.name: Design & Make Project
topics.blurb: A sustained project applying all designing and making principles

connections.why: Broad material knowledge is deepened in the chosen in-depth specialism
Emerging technologies and sustainability shape how materials are selected and used
Electronic control and mechanical devices combine in many working products
Smart and composite materials extend the core understanding of material properties
Research findings are turned into a design brief and specification
The specification directs the generation and development of ideas
Developed ideas are realised as a manufactured prototype
Prototypes are tested and evaluated against the specification
Evaluation feeds back into iterative refinement of design ideas
In-depth material skills determine how the prototype is manufactured
Material properties govern appropriate manufacturing processes
The full designing-and-making cycle is brought together in the NEA project
The chosen material specialism is applied throughout the NEA project
